thesis: Trim, but do not abandon, the September 29 event-driven reset through the October 13 settled session. VRTX and NEM still have falsifiable company-confirmed catalysts: Newmont reports Q3 after the October 22 close, Vertex reports Q3 after the November 2 close, and Vertex has a November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date. However, VRTX fell 4.30% on October 13 and NEM fell 1.33% while SPY fell only 0.01%. The persisted analyst book is down 15.8% versus SPY up 3.7%, or -19.5 points of alpha, with a -3.37 annualized Sharpe. The full-universe screen is also crowded: MRNA gained 50.41% over 20 sessions and 263.51% over 60; SHOP, PLTR, and several software leaders trade at premium or negative earnings multiples. Robinhood data shows VRTX at 28.229339x trailing earnings and NEM at 14.595987x. Reduce VRTX to 16%, NEM to 14%, and hold 70% cash. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve lists a two-day FOMC meeting for October 27-28, 2026, with a press conference on October 28.
Vertex says FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept in IgAN.
Vertex says it will report Q3 2026 results on November 2 after market close and host its call at 4:30 p.m. ET.
Newmont says it will release Q3 2026 results after market close on October 22 and hold its call at 5:30 p.m. EDT.
Robinhood's October 14 data shows VRTX at 28.229339x P/E, $125.2512 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target.
Robinhood's October 14 data shows NEM at 14.595987x P/E, $118.6874 billion market cap, Q2 revenue $6.118 billion, Q2 net income $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target.
At the October 13 settled close, VRTX was $485.22, NEM was $115.59, and SPY was $778.01; VRTX fell 4.30%, NEM fell 1.33%, and SPY fell 0.01% from October 12.

risks: VRTX faces a binary November 30 FDA decision; a delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation breaks the thesis.
Vertex's sharp October 13 decline may reflect information not captured by the scheduled-catalyst framework.
NEM is below the paper entry; gold-price reversal, cost inflation, or weak Q3 production can overwhelm the valuation case.
A 70% cash balance creates substantial opportunity cost if risk assets continue higher.
The persisted portfolio alpha is -19.5 points with a -3.37 annualized Sharpe; confidence stays low until realized results improve.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] FDA assigned a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date for povetacicept, and Vertex confirmed Q3 results for November 2. The October 13 close was $485.22; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 28.229339/6.071210, Q2 revenue of $3.3339 billion, Q2 net income of $1.0998 billion, and a $575.9259 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Approval can establish a nephrology franchise faster than the market credits, but the 4.30% one-day decline, binary outcome, and negative portfolio alpha require trimming the anchor from 20% to 16%. [DATA] Buy limit $490.07, about 1% above the settled close.
rationale.NEM: [DATA] Newmont confirmed Q3 results after the October 22 close; Robinhood's earnings calendar shows a $1.93 EPS estimate. The October 13 close was $115.59; Robinhood reported P/E/PB of 14.595987/3.473310, Q2 revenue of $6.118 billion, Q2 net income of $2.202 billion, and a $139.8879 mean analyst target. [ASSUMED] Stable production and costs could produce a favorable result versus the $1.93 consensus, but the decline below paper entry and commodity risk require trimming from 16% to 14%. reflection.looking_back: Before the October 13 tick, the persisted book was down 15.8% versus SPY up 3.7%, or -19.5 points of all-time alpha, with a -3.37 annualized 42-session Sharpe. On October 13, VRTX fell 4.30%, NEM fell 1.33%, and SPY fell 0.01%; at prior target weights the two positions reduced marked equity by about 1.07%, underperforming SPY by about 1.06 points.
worked: The 64% cash buffer materially reduced the October 13 damage relative to a fully invested two-name book.
VRTX and NEM retain company-confirmed, dated catalysts, so both theses remain falsifiable rather than momentum extrapolations.
missed: Both holdings materially underperformed SPY on October 13, led by VRTX's 4.30% decline.
The prior allocation was still too large for a book with -19.5 points of all-time alpha and a -3.37 Sharpe.
reflection.adjustment: Cut VRTX from 20% to 16%, cut NEM from 16% to 14%, lower confidence from 0.31 to 0.29, and raise cash from 64% to 70% until the October and November catalysts validate the positions.
